checklist.detail: NARloy-Z Copper Alloy (Cu-Ag-Zr): computed wall temp 944 K EXCEEDS its 800 K max service temp (Tc 3606 K, regenerative cooling). Marginal/unsuitable as designed. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~6.4 kW/m2K incl. carbon-deposit credit, coolant ~35 m/s (h_c ~29.8 kW/m2K, coolant-side wall ~877 K), 1.50 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.

checklist.detail: Near the end of active cooling (area ratio ~21.4), estimated jacket/coolant pressure (~13.4 MPa) exceeds local hot-gas static pressure (~0.0 MPa) - the net load on the channel-land wall there REVERSES direction. Modeled as a clamped-strip bending stress across the ~9.8 mm channel width, this reversed ~13.3 MPa differential is ~2542 MPa against a ~133 MPa allowable (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5) - but this is a coarse clamped-plate-strip proxy, NOT a real buckling/FEA analysis, and this codebase has no real-engine spot check for it yet. Treat this as 'worth a closer structural look', not a validated failure prediction. Consider more/narrower channels (smaller span), tapering the actively-cooled length, or a thicker wall there.
